sources.source_name: NBER: Business Cycle Dating Committee announcement
sources.notes: Dated announcement identifies March 2001 business-cycle peak. Event marker is announcement month, not an assertion investors knew the recession start in March.

sources.source_name: NBER: Business Cycle Dating Committee announcement
sources.notes: Dated retrospective announcement identifies November 2001 trough and beginning of expansion; identification occurred well after the turning point.
Policy target raised from 1% to 1.25%; statement describes solid output expansion. Annotation supplies context, not a causal model of returns.

sources.source_name: Microsoft: Strong Fourth Quarter Earnings, Fiscal 2004
sources.notes: Contemporary earnings release: fiscal 2004 revenue $36.84 billion and net income $8.17 billion; Windows Server 2003 and Office demand; Sun settlement and European Commission fine. The stock summary does not treat the proposed July special dividend as already paid.

Contemporary release: sharp reversal in orders, technology capital-spending weakness, $2.2 billion excess-inventory charge and $2.69 billion GAAP quarterly loss. Distinguishes inventory write-down from the separate $1.17 billion restructuring charge.

sources.source_name: Cisco: Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2004 Earnings
sources.notes: Fiscal 2004 revenue $22.0 billion (+16.8%) and GAAP net income $4.4 billion versus $3.6 billion the prior year. Records an operating recovery while scenario return paths remain below their late-1999/2000 starting prices.

sources.source_name: Amazon: 2003 Results and Year-Round Free Shipping
sources.notes: Fiscal 2003 sales $5.264 billion (+34%), net income $35 million versus a $149 million 2002 loss, operating income $271 million. Lower prices and year-round free shipping were central strategies; international sales exceeded $2 billion.
